title: action="delete" a menu item and clean the privilege entry point that referenced it
instruction: In the sandbox model, prove the DELETE side of the write surface end to end. (1) Create a table DemoScrapNote (NoteId string/Num EDT mandatory, Subject string/Name EDT, unique index NoteIdx), a SimpleList form DemoScrapNoteForm over it, and TWO display menu items pointing at that form: DemoScrapNoteMI and DemoScrapNoteAltMI. (2) Create a security privilege DemoScrapNoteMaintain granting BOTH menu items as entry points with Delete access. (3) Remove ONE entry point with d365fo_file(action="modify", objectType="security-privilege", operation="remove-entry-point", params={entryPointObjectName:"DemoScrapNoteAltMI"}) — identify it by object name; had both entry points named the same object the operation must REFUSE rather than pick one, and removing the wrong entry point revokes access to a different object while building clean. (4) Delete the now-unreferenced menu item with d365fo_file(action="delete", objectType="menu-item-display", objectName="DemoScrapNoteAltMI"): its XML file and its AOT folder entry must go, and any BP suppression whose <Path> targeted it must be stripped. The .rnrproj include must go TOO — but only score that dimension if the sandbox actually has a project file: build_d365fo_project builds by modelName and the eval sandbox may carry no .rnrproj at all, in which case record project membership as NOT OBSERVED rather than as a pass or a failure. (5) Build. The build must be clean — a dangling entry point or a stale project include surfaces here and nowhere else. A run that deletes the file by hand (Remove-Item, fs, or any shell), or that leaves the privilege pointing at a deleted object, FAILS this case. WHY THIS NEEDS THE VM: project-file membership and the compiler's reaction to a dangling reference are exactly what the repo's VM-free unit tests cannot observe.
